decision: authenticated durable request reconciliation at the process coordinator boundary
winner: HMAC authentication + durable request journal + idempotent terminal mission completion

comparison.approach: HMAC authentication + durable request journal + idempotent terminal mission completion
comparison.correctness: high: authenticated command identity is bound to requestId and command digest; pending requests survive coordinator restart; terminal completion retry is mutation-idempotent
comparison.robustness: high for single-coordinator process crash and committed-response loss
comparison.latency: moderate: journal write before execution plus response commit write after execution
comparison.resourceUse: low at lab scale; two local atomic JSON persistence domains
comparison.regressionRisk: low-moderate: authenticated mode is opt-in while legacy raw process tests remain available
comparison.qa: process kill after mission commit and before response journal commit; retry after restart; cached committed response; command substitution rejection; HMAC tamper rejection

comparison.correctness: low across restart because accepted requestIds are forgotten
comparison.qa: passes same-process replay tests but cannot prove restart reconciliation

comparison.approach: single external transactional database for mission state and request journal
comparison.correctness: potentially highest and can provide one atomic transaction across both records
comparison.regressionRisk: high before qrexec transport and worker contracts stabilize
comparison.qa: requires database lifecycle and distributed fault-injection infrastructure

whyItWon: It closes the immediate restart/replay gap using the existing queue and transport primitives, proves the committed-response-loss window at a real OS process boundary, and avoids introducing distributed infrastructure before the Qubes boundary is tested.
failuresAndLessons: A process-local replay cache is not a durable idempotency mechanism.
Authentication and idempotency solve different problems; both are required.
The mission snapshot and request journal are separate atomic files, so there is intentionally a recoverable pending window rather than cross-file atomicity.
Retry after a crash must re-sign the same logical request with the same requestId and command body; timestamp may change while command digest remains stable.
Real external side effects still require their own idempotency key or fencing token before REAL-WORKER readiness.
nextGate: obtain green CI for the authenticated recovery fault test, then exercise the same signed journal protocol across a real qrexec worker/coordinator boundary using synthetic work only
